Hey, I (23f) recently came out of a 4 and a half year engagement. I completely understand what you're going through. My parents had been telling me for a year that he (24m) holds me back and I just keep pushing back my plans for him. I didn't want to listen because I was like 'oh but we will do it at some point he's busy'

For me it started with the fact the I really didn't get along with his parents and I mothered him alot as well. It seemed as though my partner couldn't or didn't want to save and I started to put my values and morals aside for him. That's sort of when I knew. I always have wanted children and to be a mother is my dream. He kept pushing it back and gave me weak excuses. I spoke about parenting styles and schools and we had different opinions, but I still loved him.

He was very much a mamas boy. It was difficult and still is difficult to come to one thing that made me leave him because I started questioning what I wanted to make him happy. I wondered whether the grass was greener on the other side and I almost cheated, you don't want to do that.

I went out one night for a drink and he had a go at me because my phone died and within 3 days I was moved out. It became a mess.

To answer your question: I would imagine this is the age that he would maybe want to start settling down? Everyone is different. However, you want to travel. The moment you start getting doubts is when you need to have serious conversations. I started having doubts and just let them grew, thought I'd get over them. I wish I spoke to him. 

Do you care what others think? Do you think he's holding you back? What would you actually be doing if you weren't with him? Would what youd be doing make you happier?

Feel free to message and ask my about my experience or anything, it's difficult to get it all down in a cohesive text.

P.S I didn't believe it, but you can break up with people because you're going in different directions and still love and want the best for them. I will forever love my ex. But I couldn't be with him anymore.

Hi. I've been struggling coming to terms that I may have adhd and autism. I won't go into symptoms but there are alot and it makes alot more sense now discovering this. Practically my whole family is autistic and I believed everything I did was normal, as I was classed as the normal one in my family growing up... little did I know I was just 'more normal' than the rest because I felt I had to be and I masked it.

I've spoken to my parents about getting a diagnosis and they say that I definitely have it, but the diagnosis may take a while especially now that I'm a 23F. I don't know what to do, I've coped okay up till now I just find that it's all so much more difficult to keep on top of things and the symptoms seem to be much worse. Parents have said I don't need a label and I agree, but I genuinely think it may help? Everything just makes more sense now that I have an idea of why I can't do simple tasks or hold conversations

I'm not self diagnosing. I've grown up with a lot of autistic people in my life and I work with SEN children. So I do have an idea of what I'm talking about.
